# Frozen acceptance-path tests

S1.1-3 and S1.1-9, with the D4 default assumption. This is a test-only
handoff: no engine, CLI, schema, template or runner-harness change.

## Boundaries

The matrix reuses a fixture repository per test thread wherever only runtime
state changes; integration and audit-only cases get fresh disposable repositories.
There are no remotes. G/A/D/E are established using the shipped verification binding,
review-ledger and evidence-manifest writers, and checked by the shipped
acceptance program before V is varied. The host gate is `true`; the distinct
proof command is `bash proof.sh` and its declared proof file is `proof.sh`.
That command fails on the base (no widget) and passes on the candidate.

Each of the nine paths has missing-proof enforcement, valid-proof, `off`,
`observe`, and default red-proof / explicit `driver-only` controls:

* Ordinary publication executes the verbatim driver suffix from its acceptance
  predicate through inbox publication. Its real top-level functions are loaded
  using Bash's parser, as in the frozen red-proof phase fixture. Only status UI
  rendering is replaced. Gate/audit/provider preparation is outside this seam;
  real packet, task, lease, event, decision and inbox writes remain inside it.
* Retained-checkpoint resume and stranded-packet heal use `drive TASK-0001`.
  The latter disables `SINGULAR_RESUME_ACCEPTED_EVIDENCE` so it cannot silently
  exercise the first route twice.
* `drive --audit-only` uses its public resume record and a local auditor. The
  predecessor has no completed review round, matching an unreadable audit.
  A Python executable observer installs or removes the fixture proof just
  before the real acceptance program runs, after any earlier proof phase.
  It forwards every invocation unchanged and never returns an acceptance
  answer. This isolates final acceptance from the earlier producer's refusal.
  The test requires that this seam was reached and no implementer ran.
* Import runs the bundled `engine/import-packet.sh` entrypoint.
* Integration uses `singular integrate`; the explicit `integrate --task` retry
  first integrates the candidate and then retries that exact accepted run.
* `recover candidate --action regate` starts with a retained certificate and
  an infrastructure failure written by the real lifecycle program.
* `accept-packet` starts from a pending packet with valid independent evidence.

Strict failures must exit nonzero, identify V, publish no accepted inbox
packet, and leave the target unchanged. Additional assertions cover pending
packet status, imported certificate absence, and recovery authority absence.
Already accepted historical records are allowed to remain historical; they
must not become fresh publication authority after proof deletion.

## Proof contract and adversarial cases

Records use `singular.orchestration.red-proof.v0` and exactly the required
bindings/observations frozen in `rp-step.t` (5214d2e), plus task/run identities.
The fixture filename is `red-proof-attempt-1.json`; removal discovers records
by schema, including records generated by the earlier proof phase. The
fixture's logs are explicitly synthetic. These are acceptance-input fixtures,
not claims of host evidence for the product. They do not prescribe how the
producer computes proof. Settings are unexported shell configuration values,
so the real callers must pass their resolved values into Python.

The independent record matrix removes V inputs one at a time: missing record,
non-proved outcomes (including a strict waiver), wrong base/head/tree/attempt,
command identity/hash, proof-file hash/omission, both log hashes, and incorrect
base/candidate observations. A previously accepted answer cannot cache away
proof deletion. Characterization and both predeclared waiver policies have
positive controls and missing-record refusals; a task declaring neither proof
field keeps the original rule. The separate declares-nothing parity test pins
full-run bytes and remains unchanged.

Remove the V guard or ignore its result at any boundary: that path's
`enforce/every-path/missing` case fails. Remove a binding/outcome check: its
named record-matrix case fails. Fail closed on every proof indiscriminately:
valid-proof and policy controls fail. Enforce while off/observing: compatibility
controls fail. S1.1-9 is exercised by ordinary publication after an accepted
answer and by explicit integration retry after successful integration.

Short numbered case directories keep the evidence broker below the AF_UNIX
path limit. At most two fixture jobs run. Every subprocess has a deadline; no fixed sleep,
provider, network call, autonomous loop, installed engine or remote is used.
Repositories ignore runtime state. The outer shell captures and unsets Rails
verdict variables before starting any child, cleans up, and writes the nonce
only as its final successful action. No green implementation or guard-removal
result is claimed by this test-author row; those remain the builder's work.
